setup.intro: Set up the hub in four steps. Each is saved as soon as it is done.
setup.consoleOnly: Setup is done in the browser on the hub computer.

person.title: 1. Your name

person.label: Your name
person.error: Use 1 to 64 characters, without control characters.

site.title: 2. Radio
site.surveyHint: The hub listens on each channel through the first gateway, which takes about six minutes. A gateway must be connected.
site.rateHint: Lower is slower and reaches further; higher is faster and shorter. Fixed once the first device is paired.

wifi.title: 3. Wi-Fi for devices
wifi.intro: Sirens and Wi-Fi gateways join this network. The hub keeps the password and gives it only to the boards you add; it is entered here, on the hub computer, so it does not cross the home network.

devices.title: 4. Devices
devices.intro: Plug the gateway in first: it is added on its own. Then add sensors and sirens over USB and name them.

groups.intro: A group is a set of sensors and the sirens they sound. A sensor may be in several groups. A sensor in no group sounds every siren.
groups.name: Group name

groups.atLeastOneSiren: Choose at least one siren, or Every siren.
groups.soundsEvery: Every siren sounds for this group.
groups.noneLeft: None of this group's sirens is left, so every siren sounds for it.

modes.intro: A mode is a set of groups: switching to it arms their sensors and disarms the others. Away and Disarmed are fixed.
modes.name: Mode name
modes.noGroups: There are no groups yet: make one first.
modes.fixed: A fixed mode: it cannot be changed or deleted.
modes.deleteCurrentQuestion: {{name}} is the current mode. Delete it? The house stays armed as it is, in no mode.

schedules.intro: Each entry does one thing at one time, in the hub's time zone ({{zone}}). A missed entry is skipped, never run late.

schedules.name: Entry name

noTargets.mode: No modes are known to this browser yet.

failure.unreachable: The hub cannot be reached from this phone. Check that the phone is on the home Wi-Fi.
failure.refused: The hub does not know this code: it may have been used, have expired, or be mistyped.
failure.wrongHub: This is not the hub that made the code, so nothing was sent to it.
failure.notAccepted: The hub did not accept the code. It may be mistyped, used or expired.
failure.needsName: The hub needs your name to link this phone.
failure.protocol: The hub's answer could not be read.
failure.timeout: The hub did not answer in time.
failure.noWebCrypto: This phone could not make its key, so it cannot be linked.
failure.extractable: This phone could not make its key, so it cannot be linked.
failure.failed: This phone could not make its key.
failure.notBuilt: This phone cannot link yet: linking is still being built for phones.
failure.storage: This phone could not keep its key, so it is not linked.
failure.unreadable: The link held a code that could not be read. Ask for a new one.
failure.badCode: That code is not right: check it and type it again.

code.unreadable: This code could not be read. Ask for a new one.
code.notHome: This code names an address outside your home network, so this phone does not use it.
code.notLink: This code does not link a phone. Type the code the hub computer or a linked phone shows.

phoneRestore.title: Restore a hub
phoneRestore.phoneOnly: A hub is restored on the hub computer, unlocked by a phone that holds its backup key.
phoneRestore.noKey: This phone does not hold the key for that backup. Use a phone that was linked to that home on {{date}}.
phoneRestore.done: Restored. {{home}} is starting again, and this phone reaches it by itself.
phoneRestore.notRestoreCode: This code links a device. Scan the restore code on the new hub computer.

fault.unreachable: The new hub cannot be reached from this phone. Check that the phone is on the home Wi-Fi.
fault.refused: The new hub does not know this code: it may have been used or have expired. Start again on the hub computer.
fault.wrongHub: This is not the hub that made the code, so nothing was sent to it.
fault.notAccepted: The new hub did not take this phone's answer. Start again on the hub computer.
fault.storage: This phone could not read its backup keys.
fault.protocol: The new hub's answer could not be read.
fault.timeout: The new hub did not answer in time.
fault.noKey: This phone does not hold the key for that backup. Use a phone that was linked to that home when the backup was made.

notFound.title: There is no such page
notFound.body: The app has no page at that address.

failed.title: This page could not be shown
failed.body: Something went wrong while showing it. Try again; if it fails again, close the app and open it again.

vault.locked: This phone has restarted and has not been unlocked since, so the app cannot read its key yet. Unlock the phone; the app tries again when you come back to it.
vault.denied: The phone refused the app its secure storage, so the app cannot use its key. Restart the phone and open the app again.
vault.corrupt: The key this phone kept for your home could not be read back. Link this phone again from another phone or the hub computer.
vault.full: This phone is out of storage, so the app could not save what it needs. Free some space, then try again.
vault.failed: The app could not use this phone's secure storage. Try again; if it keeps failing, restart the phone.

sirens.everyWillSound_one: {{groups}} will then have none of its own sirens left, so every siren will sound for it.
sirens.everyWillSound_other: {{groups}} will then have none of their own sirens left, so every siren will sound for them.
sirens.gone_one: {{siren}} was removed or reset, so {{groups}} has none of its own sirens left, and every siren will sound for it.
sirens.gone_other: {{siren}} was removed or reset, so {{groups}} have none of their own sirens left, and every siren will sound for them.
sirens.goneNoGroups: {{siren}} was removed or reset, so a group was left with none of its own sirens, and every siren sounds for it. Groups says which sirens sound for each.
